question: Under section 19(3) of the Code on Wages, what opportunity must be given before imposing a fine?
expected_conditions: The employee must have an opportunity to show cause against the fine.
source_quote:
No fine shall be imposed on any employee until such employee has been given an
opportunity of showing cause against the fine
review_notes: Assistant-created candidate; no independent review or holdout run.

question: Under section 19(4) of the Code on Wages, what is the maximum fine for one wage period?
expected_conditions: No more than three per cent of the wages payable for that wage period.
source_quote:
The total amount of fine which may be imposed in any one wage-period on any
employee shall not exceed an amount equal to three per cent. of the wages payable to him in
respect of that wage-period.
review_notes: Assistant-created candidate; no independent review or holdout run.

question: Under section 19(6) of the Code on Wages, what limits apply to recovery of a fine?
expected_conditions: A fine cannot be recovered by instalments or after ninety days from the day it was imposed.
source_quote:
No fine imposed on any employee shall be recovered from him by instalments or
after the expiry of ninety days from the day on which it was imposed.
review_notes: Assistant-created candidate; no independent review or holdout run.

question: Under section 6(1) of the Industrial Relations Code, how many Trade Union members can apply for registration?
expected_conditions: Seven or more members may apply, subject to subscribing their names to the rules and complying with the registration provisions.
source_quote:
Any seven or more members of a Trade Union may, by subscribing their names
to the rules of the Trade Union and by otherwise complying with the provisions of this
Code with respect to registration, apply for registration of the Trade Union under this
Code.
review_notes: Assistant-created candidate; no independent review or holdout run.

question: Under section 6(4) of the Industrial Relations Code, what ongoing membership threshold must a registered workers’ Trade Union meet?
expected_conditions: At least ten per cent of connected workers or one hundred workers, whichever is less, subject to a minimum of seven.
source_quote:
A registered Trade Union of workers shall at all times continue to have not less
than ten per cent. of the workers or one hundred workers, whichever is less, subject to a
minimum of seven, engaged or employed in an industrial establishment or industry with
which it is connected, as its members.
review_notes: Assistant-created candidate; no independent review or holdout run.

question: How does the Code on Social Security define sickness?
expected_conditions: A condition requiring medical treatment and attendance and necessitating abstention from work on medical grounds.
original_title: The Code on Social Security, 2020 (No. 36 of 2020)
source_quote:
"sickness" means a condition which requires medical treatment and attendance
and necessitates abstention from work on medical ground;
review_notes: Assistant-created candidate; no independent review or holdout run.

question: How does the Code on Social Security define retirement?
expected_conditions: Termination of an employee’s service otherwise than on superannuation.
original_title: The Code on Social Security, 2020 (No. 36 of 2020)
source_quote:
"retirement" means termination of the service of an employee otherwise than on
superannuation;
review_notes: Assistant-created candidate; no independent review or holdout run.
